name: C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) / Content Credentials -- technical specification for cryptographically signed provenance metadata, currently at v2.x (fast-tracked as ISO/DIS 22144; v1 adopted into JPEG Trust ISO/IEC 21617-1:2025); critiqued in 'Verifying Provenance of Digital Media: Why the C2PA Specifications Fall Short' (arXiv:2604.24890).
kind: Open industry standard (standards-track specification), governed by a multi-stakeholder coalition (Adobe, Microsoft, BBC, camera/publisher members etc.), with an accompanying academic critique paper providing the independent-evaluation half of this item.
maturity: Mature and standards-track: v1.0 through v2.4 released, v2 fast-tracked to ISO/DIS 22144, v1 folded into ISO/IEC 21617-1:2025 (JPEG Trust). Actively extended -- v2.4 specifically ADDED support for embedding manifests into HTML documents and into 'structured text formats (source code, YAML, Markdown, AsciiDoc, etc.)', which is directly relevant to this project since it means the spec now explicitly contemplates markdown as a manifest-bearing format, not just images/video/audio.
license: Specification itself is openly published (spec.c2pa.org) under the coalition's open-standard terms; implementations (open-source SDKs, WASM verifiers like 'Content Credentials Verify' and 'C2PA Viewer') are separately licensed, not independently confirmed per-implementation in this pass. Permits use in this project as a reference specification without licensing obstruction.
keeps_and_discards: C2PA keeps a MANIFEST (a data structure recording ASSERTIONS -- facts about origin, creation tool, edit history, and 'ingredients'/source assets incorporated into the work) cryptographically signed via PKI and either HARD-bound (cryptographic hash uniquely identifying the entire asset or a portion of it) or SOFT-bound (a non-unique fingerprint or invisible watermark) to the content. For TEXT/structured-text content specifically, the mechanism KEEPS the manifest as a sequence of non-rendering UNICODE VARIATION SELECTORS embedded inline in the text itself (for unstructured text) -- a mechanism this project should note carefully given its own Unicode-sanitization concerns elsewhere in this research set, since it means a legitimate C2PA-embedded manifest and a malicious Unicode-based obfuscation payload use structurally similar techniques (invisible non-rendering codepoints). It DISCARDS any notion of verifying the TRUTH of the asserted facts -- the manifest attests that 'tool X declared certain information,' not that the information is true (a limitation the spec itself does not hide).
structure_preserved: For HARD binding, the hash can cover 'the entire asset or a PORTION thereof' -- meaning fragment-level/partial-content attestation is architecturally supported in principle, though whether this extends to DOM-subtree-level attestation of a web page (as opposed to whole-document or whole-media-file attestation) was not confirmed from available sources. The v2.4 HTML-embedding addition's exact mechanism (meta tags vs. comments vs. sidecar) was not confirmed from available (non-paywalled, non-JS-rendered) spec-page fetches in this pass.
interactive_elements: Not addressed -- C2PA's asset model is document/media-centric (images, video, audio, text/code documents), with no confirmed notion of interactive-control state as part of its assertion vocabulary.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not applicable -- outside C2PA's scope entirely.
layout_awareness: Not applicable -- C2PA operates on the ASSET/file level (or fragment-of-asset via hard binding), not on rendered layout/geometry.
javascript_required: Not applicable to the specification itself; verification tools (Content Credentials Verify, C2PA Viewer) run client-side via WebAssembly specifically so 'files never leave the user's device,' which makes offline/air-gapped verification possible -- a design choice worth noting as a privacy-positive pattern (verification without a server round-trip) independent of C2PA's broader applicability to this project.
evaluation_method: The specification itself is not empirically 'evaluated' in the benchmark sense; the independent-evaluation half of this item is the arXiv:2604.24890 critique paper, which analyzes the SPECIFICATION's security properties (not a corpus of captured data) and identifies structural/architectural weaknesses rather than running a quantitative attack-success study against sample manifests (no denominator-bearing numeric results were confirmed from available sources -- the paper reads as an architectural/security analysis, not an empirical benchmark).
corpus_size_and_origins: Not applicable in the corpus sense -- C2PA is a specification, and its critique paper is an architectural analysis rather than a corpus-based study. No page/sample counts to report.
reported_precision_recall: Not applicable -- no precision/recall-style metric exists for a cryptographic-attestation specification; the relevant question is binary verifiability (does a signature check pass) plus the qualitative trust-chain questions the critique paper raises (see independent_oracle and failure_modes).
independent_oracle: This is exactly the critique paper's core finding, phrased as C2PA's own limitation: the specification provides NO independent oracle for the FIRST-MILE trust question -- 'C2PA proves a file was signed by a specific device or software, but cannot verify that the camera was pointed at what it purports to show' (or, for this project's analogue, that a captured page's manifest-asserted metadata reflects what a browser ACTUALLY rendered, as opposed to what the capturing tool merely claims). The critique paper frames this as 'the system assumes trustworthy first signers without cryptographic enforcement at the capture stage' -- i.e. C2PA verifies the CHAIN of custody after the first signature, but the first signature itself is an act of trust, not verification.
evidence_independence: The specification is coalition-governed (multi-stakeholder, including camera/software vendors with a direct commercial interest in the standard's adoption -- Adobe, Microsoft, camera manufacturers), so the SPEC's own documentation is not independent of its backers' interests, though the coalition's broad, competitive membership provides some balance. The critique paper (arXiv:2604.24890) is independent academic security research, explicitly adversarial in its framing ('Why the C2PA Specifications Fall Short'), giving this item a genuinely independent second opinion rather than relying solely on the standard's own self-description.
page_archetype_coverage: Not applicable -- C2PA's scope is asset-type-based (image/video/audio/document/text/code), not page-structural-archetype-based in the WCXB sense.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Not directly addressed for language/script diversity, though the Unicode-Variation-Selector embedding mechanism for unstructured text has a LATENT script-interaction risk worth flagging: variation selectors are themselves Unicode codepoints with defined behavior in COMBINING-CHARACTER contexts, and their interaction with complex scripts (CJK variation selectors are a real, distinct Unicode feature already used for legitimate glyph selection in some scripts) was not addressed in available sources -- a potential collision/ambiguity between C2PA's REPURPOSED use of variation selectors as an invisible data channel and any LEGITIMATE use of variation selectors already present in scanned multilingual text.
leaks_outward: Not a primary concern of the specification (manifests are designed to be visible/verifiable metadata, not secrets), though the specification's own admission that manifests can encode 'who or what created the content... when and where it was created' means a captured/re-published page carrying a C2PA manifest could inadvertently disclose CAPTURE-TIME metadata (location, tool identity, timestamp) that this project's own privacy posture would want to review before ever attaching or propagating such a manifest.
mechanism_detectability: Directly relevant and double-edged: the OPPOSITE of most items in this research set, C2PA WANTS its mechanism to be openly detectable/verifiable (that is the entire point of a provenance standard) -- but the unstructured-text embedding technique (invisible non-rendering Unicode Variation Selectors sequence) is, by construction, INVISIBLE to a casual reader/renderer even though it is intentionally verifiable by a C2PA-aware tool. This means from a THIRD PARTY's perspective (not the page's own perspective), the mere presence of invisible non-rendering Unicode content in captured text is AMBIGUOUS between a legitimate C2PA manifest and a malicious payload, unless the tool specifically parses for C2PA's known manifest structure -- directly relevant to this project's own Unicode-sanitization item, since a blanket 'strip all non-rendering Unicode' policy would also strip legitimate C2PA provenance data.
countermeasures: Not a countermeasure system itself -- C2PA IS the countermeasure (against unattributed/unverifiable content), and its own documented weaknesses (see failure_modes) are the things that would need separate countermeasures: 'strip attacks' are mitigated only by re-verification failing gracefully (absence-of-manifest correctly read as 'no verifiable provenance,' NOT as 'proven fake' -- the spec is explicit that 'the absence of a manifest does not prove a file is fake, only that it lacks verifiable provenance,' an important asymmetry).
measured_fidelity_cost: Not applicable in a numeric sense -- no measured cost/benefit tradeoff was confirmed from available sources; the closest analogue is the qualitative tradeoff between HARD binding (cryptographically robust, but requires embedding into the asset, which can be stripped by re-encoding/re-saving through a non-C2PA-aware tool -- 'a non-C2PA tool can save a JPEG without the manifest container, silently removing all credentials') and SOFT binding (survives some transformations via fingerprint/watermark robustness, but is 'not statistically unique,' i.e. weaker identity guarantee).
gate_state_at_capture: Not addressed by the specification directly, though C2PA's action-assertion vocabulary (c2pa.created, c2pa.opened, c2pa.watermarked.bound, and by extension whatever HTML/text-capture-specific actions v2.4 defines) is STRUCTURALLY the right place to record capture-context metadata like gate state if this project wanted to adopt a C2PA-STYLE (not necessarily C2PA-literal) assertion for its own captures -- the spec's action vocabulary is extensible in principle, though whether a 'behind consent banner' or 'behind paywall' assertion type exists was not confirmed.
determinism: Cryptographic signature verification is deterministic given a fixed manifest and fixed key material (standard PKI properties); the underlying ASSERTIONS' truthfulness is explicitly NOT guaranteed deterministic or even truthful by the spec itself (see independent_oracle).
determinism_across_versions: Relevant and partially addressed: C2PA is versioned (v1 through v2.4+) with the v2.4 HTML/structured-text support being NEW, meaning older manifests/verifiers may not recognize newer asset types, and newer verifiers must remain backward-compatible with older manifest versions -- a real cross-version compatibility surface the spec presumably manages (per standard practice for versioned specs) but not independently confirmed with specific backward-compatibility guarantees in this pass.
reproducibility: High for the VERIFICATION step (a given manifest either passes or fails cryptographic verification deterministically), low/unaddressed for the ASSERTION-truthfulness step (re-running verification does not re-confirm truthfulness, only confirms the signature is intact and matches the claimed signer).
failure_modes: Extensively documented, both by the specification's own honest self-disclosure and by the independent critique paper: (1) STRIP ATTACKS -- a non-C2PA-aware tool can silently save/re-encode an asset without its manifest container, removing all credentials with no error or warning to the user, and critically 'eliminating evidence of prior modifications' (i.e. stripping doesn't just remove GOOD provenance, it can be used to erase a record of BAD edits); (2) FIRST-MILE TRUST -- no cryptographic enforcement that the FIRST signer's claims are true, only that they were made by that signer; (3) SOFT-BINDING SEPARABILITY -- soft-bound manifests can become 'orphaned' from their content since the binding is metadata-level, not cryptographically inseparable, per the critique paper's central architectural objection; (4) METADATA ACCURACY -- 'C2PA signing tools do not verify that metadata is accurate,' a second-order trust gap distinct from the first-mile problem (even a legitimate, non-malicious signer can attach WRONG metadata without the spec catching it); (5) PLATFORM PROCESSING -- named as 'one of C2PA's most significant real-world limitations in 2026': platforms that announced Content-Credentials display support have upload pipelines that DESTROY manifests before they can ever be shown to end users, a practical/operational failure mode independent of any cryptographic weakness in the spec itself.
failure_visibility: Mixed and important: manifest ABSENCE is correctly specified as inconclusive rather than damning ('does not prove a file is fake') -- a loud, honest failure semantics for the ABSENT case. But manifest STRIPPING is, by the critique paper's account, SILENT from the end-user's perspective (a re-saved file simply has no manifest, indistinguishable in the file itself from content that never had one) -- meaning the loud/honest absence-semantics only helps a sophisticated verifier who already expects to check for a manifest; a casual consumer sees no signal at all that stripping occurred.
scale_limits: Not addressed -- no throughput/scale claims made by the specification; it operates per-asset, not as a bulk-processing system.
delta_cost_model: Not applicable -- C2PA manifests are attached per-asset at creation/edit time, with no incremental-update cost model of the kind this project's O(delta) constraint targets; each EDIT action typically appends a new assertion to the manifest's history chain rather than re-deriving the whole manifest, which is a form of append-only-log design loosely analogous to this project's own evolution-log architecture, though not framed by C2PA in delta-cost terms.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable in the DOM sense; C2PA's closest analogue is HARD binding's ability to hash 'a portion' of an asset, which is a static, one-time content-hash operation rather than a re-anchoring mechanism that survives subsequent mutation -- if the underlying content changes, the hard-bound hash simply fails to verify rather than adapting/re-anchoring, a fundamentally different design philosophy from this project's own re-anchoring interest (C2PA wants tamper-EVIDENT rigidity; this project wants tamper-TOLERANT identity tracking).
adversarial_exposure: The strip-attack and first-mile-trust weaknesses are both directly adversarial-exposure-relevant: an adversary who wants to REMOVE true provenance (to launder manipulated content as unattributed rather than falsely attributed) can do so trivially via strip attacks, while an adversary who wants to ATTACH false-but-plausible provenance is limited only by whatever signing-key access they can obtain (the spec's PKI trust model pushes this risk to key management/certificate-authority trust, not eliminating it). Neither of these is unique to C2PA as a general property of provenance-attestation systems, but both are concretely documented HERE rather than left theoretical.
provenance_carrying: This field is the specification's entire purpose, and its answer is the most detailed, standards-grade treatment of provenance carrying in this whole research set: assertions (facts) organized into a claim (signed statement) inside a manifest (the full record), with an explicit INGREDIENTS concept (source assets incorporated into a derived work, forming a provenance CHAIN/graph, not just a flat tag) and an explicit ACTIONS vocabulary (c2pa.created, c2pa.opened, c2pa.watermarked.bound, etc.) recording the TYPE of provenance event, not just its existence. This is architecturally richer than any of the ad-hoc provenance schemes in the LLM-agent-defense literature (item 8) -- C2PA's manifest chain is closer to a proper directed graph of derivation events, which is conceptually a good REFERENCE MODEL for how this project's own trie-based provenance keys could be structured (origin url + xpath + capture time + an explicit ACTION/event type), even though C2PA's specific binary format and PKI machinery are not directly reusable.
roundtrip_safety: Directly and concretely relevant: v2.4's unstructured-text embedding mechanism (a sequence of non-rendering Unicode Variation Selectors) is EXACTLY the kind of construct this project's own roundtrip_safety / escaping-policy work (item 7) needs to reason about -- a serialize->parse->serialize fixed-point check on captured text containing an embedded C2PA manifest must either (a) preserve the invisible variation-selector sequence exactly (to keep the manifest verifiable) or (b) explicitly and intentionally strip it (accepting the tradeoff of destroying legitimate provenance along with any similarly-invisible malicious payload) -- there is no free lunch here, and this project's own escaping policy needs to make a DELIBERATE choice about which behavior it wants, informed by this tension rather than accidentally doing one or the other.
token_budget_and_ordering: Not applicable -- C2PA manifests are not designed with an SLM context-window consumer in mind; if anything, an embedded non-rendering Unicode manifest would be pure token-budget WASTE from an SLM's perspective unless the consuming pipeline specifically strips it before tokenization (another point favoring explicit, deliberate handling per roundtrip_safety above, rather than passive pass-through).
representation_cost: Not addressed in token terms, though a C2PA manifest embedded via non-rendering Unicode characters does add a nonzero BYTE cost to a text document proportional to the manifest's assertion/claim complexity -- exact size figures were not confirmed from available sources.
what_could_be_adopted: Two specific mechanisms, one conceptual reference model: (1) ADOPT THE ASSERTION/CLAIM/INGREDIENTS CONCEPTUAL MODEL (not the binary format or PKI machinery) as a reference for structuring this project's own capture-provenance metadata -- explicit ACTION-typed events (analogous to c2pa.created/c2pa.opened) attached to each capture, with an explicit chain/graph of 'ingredients' when derived content (e.g. a dedup'd or re-anchored element) traces back to multiple prior captures, is a richer and more standards-aligned model than a flat provenance tag; (2) ADOPT THE ABSENCE-IS-INCONCLUSIVE-NOT-DAMNING semantics explicitly into this project's own failure_visibility posture for any provenance field it exposes -- missing provenance should be reported as 'unknown/unverifiable,' never silently treated as either 'trusted' or 'proven malicious,' matching C2PA's own honest framing; (3) treat the Unicode-Variation-Selector embedding technique as a NEGATIVE PRECEDENT informing (not directly adopted into) this project's own escaping/sanitization policy -- knowing that a LEGITIMATE standard uses exactly the invisible-Unicode-payload technique that a naive Unicode sanitizer would strip is a concrete argument for building any sanitization policy with explicit, named exceptions/allowlisting rather than blanket stripping, and for flagging (not silently discarding) any detected non-rendering Unicode sequence so a human or downstream system can decide its disposition.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- C2PA's assertion/manifest model classifies EVENTS (created/opened/edited) and ASSET TYPES, not page REGIONS (nav/article/result); adopting its conceptual model introduces no region-naming heuristic. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- C2PA operates entirely on asset/content-hash level, never on rendered geometry. o_delta: PARTIALLY ADOPTABLE -- the manifest's append-only action-history chain is loosely delta-shaped (each edit appends an assertion rather than re-deriving the whole manifest), a genuinely useful pattern for this project's own evolution log, though C2PA itself makes no O(delta) COMPUTATIONAL COST claim, only a structural append-only design choice. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- nothing about the standard requires or encourages stubbing; its cryptographic verification is either genuinely checked against real signatures or not attempted at all. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NOT APPLICABLE, THOUGH CONCEPTUALLY CONSISTENT -- C2PA's own honest 'absence proves nothing' semantics for stripped/missing manifests is philosophically the SAME honesty this project already commits to for unreachable closed shadow roots (report unreachability honestly rather than silently omitting or falsely asserting completeness); the alignment is thematic, not a direct mechanism transfer. OVERALL VERDICT: adoptable as a CONCEPTUAL REFERENCE MODEL for provenance structuring and absence-semantics (genuinely valuable, standards-grade thinking this project's own provenance design should measure itself against), but NOT adoptable as a literal implementation (the PKI/binary-manifest machinery is built for a different threat model -- proving asset authenticity to a broad public verifier ecosystem -- than this project's own internal capture-provenance tracking needs), and the Unicode-Variation-Selector mechanism specifically should inform (as a cautionary precedent) rather than be copied into this project's escaping policy.
governance_signal_handling: Not directly a governance-signal mechanism (robots.txt/ai.txt-style), though C2PA is philosophically adjacent to the broader AI-content-governance movement (IETF AIPREF, Content Signals, etc. covered in item 12) as another piece of the same 'machine-readable trust/rights signal' infrastructure -- C2PA signals PROVENANCE, those signal PERMISSION, and a mature ecosystem would likely want both read together.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Not directly addressed by the specification, though relevant by extension: since manifests can carry creator/location/timestamp metadata, any captured content this project retains WITH an intact third-party C2PA manifest would be retaining that metadata too, subject to the same PII/lawful-basis review as any other retained personal data -- the specification itself provides no exemption or special handling for this case.
uncertain: Exact HTML-embedding mechanism added in v2.4 (meta tags vs. comments vs. sidecar file vs. some other approach) was not confirmed from available sources -- only that the capability was added
Whether hard binding supports true DOM-subtree-level (as opposed to whole-file or byte-range) fragment attestation for HTML specifically was not confirmed

The critique paper (arXiv:2604.24890)'s PDF text extraction was partially garbled; its qualitative findings were corroborated across multiple summary passes but exact quoted section numbers/page references were not independently verified against the original layout

Whether any quantitative attack-success or strip-attack-ease numbers exist in the critique paper was not confirmed -- the paper reads as primarily architectural/qualitative analysis based on available extraction

Interaction between C2PA's Unicode Variation Selector embedding and legitimate script-specific variation-selector usage (e.g. in CJK text) was reasoned by inference from Unicode's general variation-selector mechanics, not confirmed as a documented C2PA concern in the spec itself
